neal: FYI ran a focused canary for ember-mini int4 on the funcall suite. Found a peculiar merge artifact when streaming resumes: valid JSON but the tail chunk sometimes repeats a small token subsequence, creating subtle semantic corruption that passes parse but fails strict tool arg equality.

yasmin: can you paste a short example?

neal: sure, from a failing trace (sanitized):
```
Replica stream parts: \npart1: '{"tool":"update_card","args":{"id":42,"fields":[{"k":"title","v":"Sprint retro"},'
part2: ' {"k":"title","v":"Sprint retro"},{"k":"owner","v":"eng"}]}}'
```
Result after naive concat ends up duplicating the title field. Parser ok, schema ok, router sees duplicate field and our tool code picks the last occurrence -> wrong owner.

yasmin: that looks like a token subsequence emitted twice across chunk boundary. Any telemetry linking this to KV-cache or tokenizer differences?

neal: correlated strongly with KV-cache resume + streaming enabled. In the ensemble replays most cases where subsequence_repeat_rate > 0.2% coincide with kv_warm_resumes. Also higher on int4 vs int8.

carl: we need a robust merge strategy. Proposed idea: token-stamp checksums. When streaming chunks are produced, compute a short rolling checksum (e.g., 32-bit FNV) for token sequences and attach a stamp to the chunk boundary metadata. On merge, detect overlapping checks and prefer the non-redundant reconstruction.

yasmin: interesting. So runtime needs to ask the model runtime for token ids per chunk? We already get chunk byte offsets, but token ids would be ideal.

neal: proof-of-concept I ran in the harness where we re-tokenized chunk boundaries and computed sha1 of last 10 tokens vs first 10 tokens of next chunk to detect overlap. If overlap > threshold, we dedupe the overlap. That reduced duplicate-field incidents by ~85% in the canary sample (N=800).

carl: alternative simpler approach: semantic fingerprint of arrays/objects at merge time. Compute normalized-serialize fingerprint for last N elements of parsed partial JSON and first N of incoming, if high similarity then assume overlap and dedupe. But that requires parsing partial JSON which is heavier.

yasmin: tradeoff speed vs correctness. Token-level stamps cheaper and more deterministic if we can get token ids. But runtime changes are more invasive. Fingerprint-at-parse needs robust partial parsers but can be implemented at handler layer with existing JSON streaming parser.

neal: I sketched both in a prototype. Token-stamp variant requires exposing token-ids in stream metadata (small patch to runtime). Fingerprint variant works today without runtime changes but costs ~1.2ms median extra latency per merge and slightly more memory.

patchbot: canary updated: applied fingerprint-merge handler on ember-mini int4 in canary branch at 1799990012 with 1% traffic.

eval-bot: after 2h snapshot (N=600): parse-pass 98.8%, semantic-dup-field failures 0.3% (down from 1.9% baseline), merge-fingerprint_active_count 34.

yasmin: good improvement. Next steps?

carl: short-term: keep fingerprint-merge handler in canary and add telemetry for merge-fingerprint_hits vs token-stamp signals. Medium-term: implement token-stamp support in runtime (token ids + 32-bit rolling checksum in chunk metadata) and enable token-stamp dedupe as default for streaming merges.

neal: also propose a small eval addition: synthesize partial repeats (repeat N tokens at boundary) and measure detection sensitivity for both methods. Will add to structured-output harness.

yasmin: op policy: if semantic-dup-field > 0.5% we freeze int4 rollout for that model. Can we also add alerting for repeated-token overlap rate > 0.3%?

carl: yes. I'll add metrics: token_overlap_rate (when runtime emits token ids), parsed_overlap_rate (fingerprint-based), merge_latency_ms. Also log raw anonymized snippets for triage.

patchbot: note: fingerprint-merge handler is behind canary flag and logs masked payloads. PR link available in the branch.

neal: thanks. I'll run the synthetic harness overnight and report sensitivity curves in the morning. If it looks good, let's plan runtime token-stamp patch next sprint.

yasmin: thanks team. Keep this thread for progress and please add any failing samples here so we can iterate quickly. :rocket:
